This approach seems to be very promising for HCC grading, by comparing this result to those obtained in a previous work of the same authors using an Artificial Neural Network, whose topology was obtained using a mono-objective genetic algorithm (Bevilacqua, Brunetti, et al., 2016). In fact, taking into account that the better performing subset of features reaches a value of 92,14%, the mean accuracy value on the test set herein obtained is slightly higher than the one reached in (Bevilacqua et al., In Press). For the sake of comparison, in Table 5 the confusion matrix obtained for the test set classification is reported, being in the best case the value of Accuracy equal to 92,86%.

In particular, the good results obtained confirm the robustness of the segmentation algorithm which is able to detect and isolate the liver, thus paving the way for the HCC segmentation. Moreover, being increased the number of considered patients with respect to the previous work, the Deep Learning approach seems to be more accurate in the HCC grading, using Convolutional Neural Networks than traditional Artificial Neural Networks. It has to be noted that the work is in progress, as the number of patients is constantly increasing.

6\. CONCLUSION

In this work, a Deep Learning approach for detection and grading of hepatocellular carcinoma based on the synthesis of a Convolutional Neural Network has been proposed and validated. In detail, by using an innovative procedure for image processing of abdominal CT slices. A novel procedure for HCC detection has been designed by considering a significant number of recruited subjects; then, a ConvNet architecture has been proposed for HCC grading, trained with an enlarged dataset with respect to the one used in (Bevilacqua et al., 2017).

The results obtained in this work show that HCC grades can be classified by using only the ROIs extracted from the arterial phase of CT images, but the identification of tumor areas requires the images from both arterial and delayed phases; in fact, the HCC wash-in and wash-out dynamic suggests that this type of lesion can be characterized by processing textural differences by considering the two most important phases in the HCC dynamic.

In conclusion, results derived from the enlarged dataset of patients demonstrate the validity of the designed image processing procedure for HCC detection and, at the same time, the robustness of the proposed Deep Learning approach for grading the HCC lesions. Further improvements will certainly include dedicated image processing algorithms to fully automate the ROIs detection and segmentation. Further improvements of performances in image segmentation will be successively developed with processing algorithms allowing the extraction of new features.

ABSTRACT

With the development of information technology, more and more people use multimedia conference system to communicate or work across regions. In this article, an ultra-reliable and low-latency solution based on Deep Learning and assisted by Cloud Computing for multimedia conference system, called UCCMCS, is designed and implemented. In UCCMCS, there are two-tiers in its data distribution structure which combines the advantages of cloud computing. And according to the requirements of ultra-reliability and low-latency, a bandwidth optimization model is proposed to improve the transmission efficiency of multimedia data so as to reduce the delay of the system. In order to improve the reliability of data distribution, the help of cloud computing node is used to carry out the retransmission of lost data. the experimental results show UCCMCS could improve the reliability and reduce the latency of the multimedia data distribution in multimedia conference system.

1\. INTRODUCTION

Multimedia Conference System (MCS in short) is an application used increasingly widely, which can provide real-time transmission of video, audio, and other data to facilitate people's communication in life and work. The demand of ultra-reliability and low-latency for multimedia conference systems has also become increasingly high. In the traditional multimedia conference system, the data distribution scheme can be used in unicast or multicast technology. With the growth of conference participants, MCS adopting unicast will receive network bandwidth limitation (Lao et al., 2005). Compared with unicast, the multicast scheme, which is a distributed concurrent transmission mode, is realized by using the intermediate nodes for distributed processing, thus becoming an efficient data transmission mechanism. IP multicast is the first proposed Internet multicast solution, but it has not been widely deployed due to many reasons such as technology and market. In order to avoid the problem of IP multicast deployment, the relevant research proposed the application layer multicast. In order to improve the stability and scalability of the multicast transmission, the researchers further put forward the seeding of the application layer based on the proxy. In overlay multicast, the proxy servers, which are deployed strategically in the Internet, become the infrastructure for building an overlay network, and the user hosts receive the multicast service by accessing the proxy server (Yang and Shang, 2013). At present, the system structure of proxy application layer multicast has gradually become one of the hot spots in the research of multicast architecture. It is also considered to be a long-term solution to the future Internet multicast (Zhang et al., 2016).

Meanwhile, with the wide application of cloud computing, there are many low cost and reliable cloud nodes on the current Internet which can be used for data distribution. In this paper, an ultra-reliable and low-latency solution assisted by Cloud Computing for multi-source multimedia conference system, called UCCMCS, is designed and implemented. In UCCMCS, there are two-tiers in its data distribution structure which combines the advantages of cloud computing. And according to the requirements of ultra-reliability and low-latency, a bandwidth optimization model is proposed to improve the transmission efficiency of multimedia data so as to reduce the delay of the system. In order to improve the reliability of data distribution, we use the help of cloud computing node to carry out the retransmission of lost data. And then performance evaluation experiments are designed to validate the performance of our UCCMCS. Compared with the solution using traditional multicast technology, the experimental results show UCCMCS could improve the reliability and reduce the latency of the multimedia data distribution in multimedia conference system. Our work sheds light for distributed application design in multimedia conference and Cloud computing.

The structure of this paper is outlined below: the related works is given in section 2. The Bandwidth problem description is presented in Section 3. In Section 4, we present a deep learning solution and optimization algorithm for Bandwidth Problem. In Section 5, we present the numerical simulations for performance evaluation. We conclude the paper in Section 6.

2\. RELATED WORKS

In recent years, some researchers have attempted to combine the cloud computing and P2P (relationship between P2P and tree-type application-layer multicast has been described above) on the purpose of improving the data-distribution performance. S. Islam proposed a border cloud infrastructure (Islam and Gregorie, 2012). Similar to CDN, the proposed infrastructure deploys many border clouds at different geographical locations to improve the efficiency of data distribution. It utilizes border clouds to enlarge the application range of cloud service on the current Internet (especially cloud services in the form of streaming media applications). However, border cloud is really hard to be widely deployed in practice. A.H. Payberah et al. proposed a cloud-assisted P2P streaming-media player system, Clive (Payberah et al., 2012). Cliver evaluates the available bandwidth capacity of the whole system and computers the quantity of resources required from cloud through the aggregation protocol based on information communication. Meanwhile, on the precondition of ensuring the service quality, the overall costs are lower. Clive is the technological combination between cloud computing and trolling P2P and aims at solving the insufficient bandwidth capability of P2P. In literature (Jin and Kwok, 2010), a cloud-assisted mobile P2P streaming-media application framework was introduced. In this framework, cloud is responsible for storage and computing-related tasks, and assists the mobile terminals in completing the data distribution. This literature discussed the optimized data block searching and scheduling algorithm. The Auto-Regressive Moving Average Mode was utilized to calculate the time of storage and computing needed by the cloud instead of mobile terminal. R. Sweha et al. proposed a CloudAngels system architecture (Sweha et al., 2011). This architecture deploys the dedicated servers (called angels) in the cloud on the purpose of assisting data distribution scheme in approaching the theoretical lower limit of minimum distribution time (MDT). Literature (Montresor and Abeni, 2011) also researched the combination of data distribution and cloud computing, and proposed a CloudCast scheme. CloudAngel dynamically puts some active helpers in swarm to optimize the data distribution. CloudCast uses only a passive helper, and the quantity of interactions between other nodes and this passive helper is strictly limited. The above two schemes are mainly designed for applications of data distribution with average instantaneity and not suitable for the real-time applications such as streaming media. Literature (Fouquet et al., 2009) analyzed the combination between cloud computing and application-layer multicast. It pointed out that using cloud virtual machine as the super node of application-layer multicast was feasible. This literature only provided the simple design for the combination between cloud computing and application-layer multicast and failed to do any relevant research on the stability of multicast. Ii is analyzed that the problem of the centralized tree optimization scheme orchestration and present an effective solution that can adapt to the dynamics of group members (Zhang et at., 2017).

3\. BANDWIDTH PROBLEM DESCRIPTION

In MCS, participants in the nodes of the upload bandwidth affect the node upload video and forward the ability of video, download bandwidth of the direct relationship between the node and node video reception ability, so participants node video viewing rate not only by the node to watch video source node upload bandwidth limits, but also by the node itself to download bandwidth restrictions. Therefore, in the MCS, the upload bandwidth and the download bandwidth of the nodes are related to the quality of video. In this section, we first assume that there is no congestion in the network. Then, we discuss the relationship between the transmission of video stream and the load bandwidth and the download bandwidth of the nodes, and the maximum value of the combined value of the user video and its theoretical upper bound (Wang et al., 2016).

All conference participants viewing the same video and the video source are referred to as a sub-conference. If the number of the video sources in a video conference is |S|, the video conference will have the same number of sub-conferences.

For the sub-conference G1, the node 1 of video source will transmit the video stream to the node 3 and node 4 at the rate of 1. 4\. DEEP LEANING SOLUTION AND OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHM

Through the establishment of the above model, we give a formal description of the bandwidth problem. In the next section, we will give an optimization model and algorithm for this problem. P2P bandwidth sharing model has been applied to the video conference with the aim of fully utilizing the bandwidth resource of the nodes. In the P2P transmission network, each node can reach any other node. In order to fully utilize the upload bandwidth of the node to retransmit the video stream, we assume that all nodes will cooperate with each other. A node can not only retransmit the viewed video to other nodes for playing but also retransmit the uninterested video to other nodes for playing. The allocation of node bandwidth will directly affect the quality of video viewing. Therefore, an in-depth analysis on the video stream transmission and the method of node bandwidth allocation will be made. It is assumed that the video conference is free from network congestion. The video stream can be divided into a number of sub-streams at any rate. The rate of video viewing is only affected by the upload bandwidth and download bandwidth of the node.

For a certain sub-conference of the video conference, the bandwidth of the node can be divided into three parts according to the transmission status of the video stream. They are the upload bandwidth for uploading the video of the node, the upload bandwidth for retransmitting the video steam viewed by the node as well as the upload bandwidth for retransmitting the uninterested (unviewed) video stream of the node.

The description of the three roles played by the upload bandwidth at a certain sub-conference of the video conference can be seen as follows.

| Figure 2. Three roles of the nodes |
| --- |
| ![Figure978-1-7998-0414-7.ch022.f02](i/ch022.f02.png) |
| --- |

A detailed analysis on the video stream transmission of the three roles has been given. The analysis is conducted on condition that only the upload bandwidth is limited. But in real cases, the download bandwidth is also limited. It is possible that the download bandwidth of a certain node is lower than the sum of the rates of the video stream transmitted to the node. As a result, the node will discard a portion of video data.

Hence, the analysis on the video conference scene in this chapter will consider the download bandwidth and upload bandwidth of the node. The analysis on the video stream transmission is as follows.

As seen in the Figure 2(a), the node i divide the video data played into many sub-streams at different rates. Those sub-streams are also transmitted to each node of the viewer sub-conference G[i] and some of other nodes. The sum of the video streams received by the node is limited by the download bandwidth of the node.

As shown in the Figure 2(b), the node i is not interested in the video of the video source k. But it can receive the video of the node i (the sum of the video streams received by the node is limited by the download bandwidth of the node). After several duplications, they will be transmitted to the nodes of the viewer sub-conference G[k] so as to help transmit the video streams of the node k. Those nodes are referred to as the helper of the sub-conference G[k].

As seen in the Figure 2(c), the node i is a viewer of the sub-conference Gk. It is responsible for duplicating the video sub-stream received several times (the sum of the video streams received by the node is limited by the download bandwidth of the node) and retransmitting them to other viewer nodes of the sub-conference G[k].

5\. SYSTEM EVALUATIONS

In this section, we introduce version 3.5 of TAXOR, the culmination of years of optimizing. Since our framework studies the deployment of linked lists, coding the virtual machine monitor was relatively straightforward. Furthermore, it was necessary to cap the popularity of the producer-consumer problem used by our method to 24 man-hours. It was necessary to cap the instruction rate used by our methodology to 110 bytes. End-users have complete control over the codebase of 30 Fortran files, which of course is necessary so that IPv7 and B-trees are generally incompatible. We now discuss our performance analysis. Our overall performance analysis seeks to prove three hypotheses: (1) that RAM speed is more important than a framework's flexible ABI when maximizing throughput; (2) that we can do little to affect a system's median latency; and finally (3) that Scheme no longer adjusts instruction rate. Only with the benefit of our system's tape drive space might we optimize for security at the cost of instruction rate. We hope that this section illuminates the enigma of complexity theory (see Figure 4).

In summary, our experimental results demonstrate UCCMCS could improve the reliability and reduce the latency of the multimedia data distribution in multimedia conference system.

6\. CONCLUSION

In this article, a deep learning solution assisted by Cloud Computing for multimedia conference system, called UCCMCS, is designed and implemented. In UCCMCS, there are two-tiers in its data distribution structure which combines the advantages of cloud computing. And according to the requirements of ultra-reliability and low-latency, a bandwidth optimization model is proposed to improve the transmission efficiency of multimedia data so as to reduce the delay of the system. In order to improve the reliability of data distribution, we use the help of cloud computing node to carry out the retransmission of lost data. And then performance evaluation experiments are designed to validate the performance of our UCCMCS. Compared with the solution using traditional multicast technology, the experimental results show UCCMCS could improve the reliability and reduce the latency of the multimedia data distribution in multimedia conference system. Our work sheds light for distributed application design in multimedia conference and Cloud computing.

# Chapter 23

A Novel Approach Using Machine Learning for Assessment of Credit Card Frauds

*   Pallavi Digambarrao Kulkarni  
    Dr. D. Y. Patil School of Engineering and Technology, India
*   Roshani Ade  
    Dr. D. Y. Patil School of Engineering and Technology, India

ABSTRACT

There are several deep learning approaches that can be applied for analyzing situations in real world problems and inventing their solution in a scientific technique. Supervised data mining methods that predicts instance values, using previously obtained results from already collected data are pretty popular due to their intelligence in machine learning area. Stream data is continuous form of data which can be handled by using incremental learning approach. Stream data learning may face several challenges in real world like concept drift or class imbalance. Concept drift occurs in non-stationary environment where data distribution generation function is dynamic in nature and has no fixed formula to predict the future data distribution nature. Neural network techniques are intelligent enough to improve performance of algorithmic systems that work in such problem domains. This chapter briefly describes how MLP technique is integrated in system so that the system becomes a complete framework for handling unbalanced data with concept drift in the incremental learning strategies.

INTRODUCTION

The fundamental activity for both human and machine learning is the knowledge acquisition. It is the ultimate objective of any learning system which in turn is expected to lead towards the wisdom of the entire system. The crude definition of data mining system is to dig massive amounts of data and extracting information out of it. The term is quite misleading as it should actually be knowledge extraction as the system is extracting processed knowledge out of raw data. Supervised systems have knowledge since it has already classified labeled data to be used as of training data. It form instructions or postulates using this already classified data and uses these assumptions to calculate the classes of forthcoming data illustrations. These approaches are attractive due to their intellect in the machine learning area. However, real world problems are quite complex and need expertize to have accurate results. There are several classification algorithms to apply on such situations such as nearest neighbor classification technique, probabilistic algorithms, entropy based classifiers, support vector machines, artificial neural networks, decision tree classifiers etc. Additionally, there are various deep learning approaches that can be applied for analyzing circumstances in real world problems and inventing their solution in a scientific technique(Polikar et al., 2001, Kulkarni, & Ade, 2014).

Real world problem consists of situations where the generated data is not static, instead it is dynamically produced and mostly this happens in the computer networks. As this is the era of internet and widespread smart devices connected to each other across the globe, huge amount of data explosion takes place in the online environment. Real challenge is to handle time factor associated with this online stream data and preserve the knowledge extracted at each time instance accordingly. Learning from such data is also known as incremental learning technique that is always fed with input data in its arrival sequence and should primarily possess following properties:

*   1\. The algorithm should gain knowledge which is additional in recent data.
*   2\. To train already present classifier, the algorithm need not access to the initial data.
*   3\. It should keep up the knowledge which it has previously learned (no catastrophic forgetting should occur).
*   4\. New data may bring in concept class.

Stream data evolves over the time period and one can observe rapid increase in the amount of data stored. Stream data mining field handles various issues associated with incremental data such as class imbalance, missing features, concept drift, concept class etc. The data may be unbalanced if it consists of few samples of one class and more data samples of another class. So this majority-minority nature of data creates new challenge to learn from it. Generally, the data generating function has some predetermined form, and if that function has not predefined format and may change over time then that particular environment is known as non-stationary environment where sudden concept drift can occur. Firsthand classes may be announced over the time in case of incremental records, such classes should be renowned and data should be clustered consequently. This issue is called as concept class problem (Polikar et al., 2001).

Logistic regression learning model is quite popular statistical model which can be used to solve several real world problems. If merged into machine learning tactic, it is perceived that this system certainly works sound. In this chapter, the concept of logistic regression learning model is used in the application of multilayer perceptron neural network and that system is incorporated in the algorithm such that it forma a complete framework to handle all the issues related to stream data mining. The clue is to use this practice by way of a mapping function that grips weight distribution of the structure in iterative manner. Neural network techniques are intelligent enough to improve performance of algorithmic systems that work in such problem domains. This chapter briefly describes how MLP (MultiLayer Perceptron Neural Network) technique is integrated in system so that the system becomes a complete framework for handling unbalanced data with concept drift in the incremental learning strategies in order to obtain more accurate results along with enhanced knowledge transformation(He et al., 2011).

BACKGROUND

There are various data mining techniques that can be used for analysing problems in real world applications and discovering their solution in a scientific manner. Supervised learning techniques use instances, which have already been pre-classified in some manner. That means each instance has a label, which recognizes the class to which it belongs. Classification is a supervised data mining technique, predicts about data values, using already known results found from data gathered in advance. Classification maps, data into groups of classes established in advance. Conventionally, the supervised learning method attempts to group the data from a static dataset, the instances of which are related to the basic distribution described by a generating function. Hence it is presumed that the dataset contains all required information for learning the pertinent concepts. However, this technique has proven impractical for many real world applications, e.g., spam identification, climate monitoring, credit card fraud detection, etc. Data is usually received over time in streams of instances and is not at hand from the beginning. Such data conventionally reaches there in two ways, first is incremental arrival or batch arrival. (Kulkarni, & Ade, 2014)

Incremental learning from stream data basically suffers from various issues. Various researchers studied issues of data stream mining in detail. But there is little attention over combined problem of concept drifts and class imbalance.

A massive amount of applications in non-stationary environments with concept drifting data sources are affected from class imbalance (e.g. Climate monitoring, spam e mail identification, credit card fraud detection, network intrusion detection system).Ensemble approaches are the one which are mostly used when handling concept drift, in addition they have been proved useful for combating class imbalance. The algorithm called as uncorrelated bagging (UCB), is based on a bagging framework that trains classifiers on a subset of the majority class instances (which is selected by some user defined threshold parameter) and the combination of all minority class examples observed so far (present + former positive instances). There are several drawbacks of this approach due to its implicit assumption. It is not a true one pass (incremental) algorithm either. Selectively Recursive Approach (SERA) learning algorithm goes for a similarity measure to choose former minority examples that are most close to those in the most recent dataset. SERA is less liable to challenges of the minority class drifting compared to UCB, and may be biased bagging, BBagging, which itself by its own raises number of sampling weights of the minority data. SERA omits instances from the present training set by what it considers as not useful by using a Mahalanobis distance measure. SERA is updated to apply an ensemble technique in. But, this technique is also not strictly single pass, as it accesses previous data. Therefore both approaches written above perform best when the minority data concept is stationary and/or the former (minority class) data can be stored for later use. Also, with a window-based approach that employs a k-NN for multi-label classification for data that includes issues like concept drift and class imbalance this can be done. All these approaches and techniques area addressed in the literature and are described below. The paper by polikar et al was the first Learn++ series and the journey continued. The Learn++.CDS and Learn++.NIE are their latest algorithms that address this problem and also covers the wide literature review related to problem domain and the experiment and results describing comparison of all these techniques.

In addition to this techniques, in this article the idea of artificial neural network is imposed in the framework. The roots of artificial neural network lies in the Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. In other words, it is the technique which has overlapping idea of machine learning intelligently. Data mining and exploration of data is the task of finding useful patterns and one of the most widely used method is classification. The task of function approximation, pattern classification are quite popular using neural networks. Remember that artificial neural networks have some issues such as parameterization, time, cost etc but still they are very well classifiers and approximators. Looking at artificial neural networks includes various things such as:

*   1\. Architecture of the network.
*   2\. Learning mechanism.
*   3\. Processing details, processing model type.

Humans perform some tasks such as face recognition, natural language understanding, sentiment analysis, vision, motor control, multitasking, driving, remembering patterns etc. really well because they are the built in features in them gifted biologically. Inspired from this capability of humans artificial neural networks are developed that try to duplicate the brain neuron structure in its architecture. The vision of the strong artificial intelligence is to develop intelligent machines that can act and perceive information like humans. So the learning ability in the artificial network can lead to pretty well knowledge transformation in the system since it establishes complete node to node network and preserves the data for future use as knowledge. There are various activation functions such as step, linear, sigmoid, and logistic functions. The learning process for supervised systems consists of following phases:

*   1\. Present the network with number inputs and their corresponding outputs.
*   2\. See that how real outputs are actually close to desired outputs.
*   3\. Update the parameter in order to meet the actual outputs to desired results,

These steps should occur iteratively until the results are desirable and sustainable. Look after the conditions of the outputs so that they should not get stuck in local minima and also should not reach to the saturation point. Hence it is very important to take care of the number of iterations (epochs) to train and test the neural network based system.

This idea is implanted in the MINE framework proposed here. Considering the cost and time required to train and test the entire neural network this system uses only the upper regression layer for weight calculation. That is, mapping function is the module which is going to cover all this in detail in next upcoming sections. For now, the different categories related to mine framework and their information that can be found in the existing literature are covered.

Non- Stationary Environments

Goals of Incremental learning can be accomplished by creating ensembles of batch classifiers, where new batch classifiers can be learned on the recent data, and then integrated by using a voting mechanism. Diverse classification algorithms are combined to form an ensemble system. There are several distinguishing parameters that contribute to fulfill required diversity that in turn inspires each learner to generate various decision boundaries.

Concept drift crops up in environment that is usually known as a non-stationary environment. In simpler terms, concept drift is change in class definition over the time. In such cases it has been assumed that at time instance t, the algorithm A is stipulated with a group of labeled samples {X0,…, Xt}, where Xi is considered as a v-dimensional vector and every sample has matching class label yj. If an unclassified sample arrives at time t+1 as Xt+1, then the algorithm is anticipated to supply a class label for Xt+1. This is a forseen label of given example. One the class label is predicted for newly arrived instance, the actual label Yt+1 and a new testing sample Xt+2 arrives so that one can continue with its testing. There is a data generating function which is responsible for creation of samples at a particular time instance and hence determining nature and distribution of data. In non-stationary environment underlying and hidden distribution function (fh) changes over time. It does not remains the same like static environments. Change in distribution function can be described using several methods (Ditzler, & Polikar, 2013). In addition with concept drift, concept class is also a scenario that comes into picture in such environments whereby addition or removal of new concept classes over the timeline is observed. So the data should be classified in appropriate classes by taking into account presence of concept class and its finding should be continuously checked (Razavi et al., 2012; Muhlbaier et al., 2009).

Class Imbalance in Non-Stationary Environment

In real world, tremendous applications in non-stationary environments suffer from class imbalance. Data is said to be unbalanced or it consists of class imbalance when it does not contain approximately equal frequency of samples from every class. This is challenging situation in many real world applications which leads to inaccurate results. Examples include climate monitoring, network intrusion detection system, spam e-mail identification, and finally credit card fraud detection. An easy solution to this issue is to have under/over sampling of majority/minority class data. But this way of balancing data has some drawbacks. However, it has been observed that the joint problem of concept drift and unbalanced data has drawn little attention from researchers across the globe. Ensemble techniques are intelligent methods that handles concept drift along with class imbalance. Learn++ family of algorithms has been progressed over the time and has been addressing various issues associated with incremental learning in each new version of Learn++. Among them, Learn++.CDS and Learn++.NIE are truly incremental i.e.one pass approaches that do not touch older data, and also handle class imbalance problem well. Learn++.CDS uses SMOTE to balance the classes and its samples. It is integration of two algorithms, Learn++.NSE and SMOTE, which are existing approaches for handling concept drift and class imbalance, respectively. SMOTE approach is a robust approach to learn from unbalanced data. Learn++.NIE is more efficient framework, which will be discussed in detail in next sections. Both the approaches are able to obtain new knowledge and preserve former wisdom about the environment and its settings, which is particularly useful for recurring concepts (e.g. spiral dataset). Learn++.NIE is an intelligent algorithm that handles class imbalance in non-stationary environment. For rebalancing the data, it implements sub-ensembles with bagging along with alternate error measures. Bagging variation is a function that smartly tackles class imbalance, it neither generates synthetic samples nor suffers from undersampling, therefore is efficient in terms of performance. This algorithmic system preferably uses f-measure formula for computation of error weights (Ditzler & Polikar, 2013; Littlestone,& Warmuth,1994)

Credit card fraud detection in the financial field is a classic example of real world problem which suffers from this incremental learning issues. In this chapter, this problem is considered as one of the application or use case for the algorithmic system that is built on it to generate results. This is very critical problem whereby distinguishing between fraud and good customers or transactions is a vial issue and does not tolerate misclassification (Kulkarni & Ade,2015). There are various data mining and statistical techniques such as support vector machines, artificial neural networks, nearest neighbor algorithms etc. developed for addressing credit risk assessment. Additionally, ensemble systems also been used for the solution of this problem (Wang & Ma, 2012).Many of them use machine learning algorithms, but the complete issues of concept drift and class imbalance are little addressed by the researchers in this area.

A complete review of incremental learning, concept drift, class imbalance and other issues associated with data stream mining is available in the survey paper by Kulkarni and Ade (2014).

Generally, the technique of credit card fraud detection is to apply some classification mechanisms on similar data of previous customers both good and bad customers to look for a relation between the characteristics and potential points of failure. One important ingredient needed to achieve this goal is to find an accurate classifier that is able to categorize new applicants or existing customers as faithful or delinquent. Due to its importance of credit risk assessment, there is a growing research stream about credit risk evaluation. First of all, many statistical models and optimization techniques, such as linear discriminant analysis logit analysis, probit analysis, linear programming, integer programming, k-nearest neighbor (KNN) came into picture.

These techniques are capable to evaluate threats in credit card system, but they have limitations. There is still room to improve the capability to distinguish between faithful and delinquent customers. Latest researchers enlighted the fact that transpiring artificial intelligence approaches like artificial neural networks, support vector machines are beneficial to statistical models and optimization methods to assess credit card faults. Although nearly all supervised learning techniques can be applied to evaluate credit card threats, some merged classifiers, which unite two or more distinct classification approaches, have proven higher accuracy to predict risks than any specific methods. Combining multiple classifiers together is also known as ensemble technique and is currently thriving in credit card fault assessment.

There is no doubt that credit card fault evaluation and modelling is one of the most critical themes in the area of economic threat regulation. In recent months, due to intense difficulties in commercial field financial crises occurred, which resulted to pay more attention to credit threat assessment in banking and monetary service. Mostly for financial organizations like banks, the capability to differentiate legal and good customers from bad ones is critical. The necessity for development of reliable model is exigent so that the relevant parties can decide what actions to take. They can go for either preventive or corrective actions based on the results of predictive models. In other words, prediction of credit risk assessment has become matter of vital care in financial industry. Correct prediction of credit faults ultimately leads towards a more systematic use of financial stock and guides how efficiently the capital can be used.

There are some general guidelines to shape up a system for learning in non-stationary environments.

*   1\. Necessity of truly incremental or one pass learning where access to previous data is strictly not allowed for future training. It means that any instance is processed only once with training and at that time only the knowledge must be retrieved and summarized so that it can be used in model building process
*   2\. It is known fact that the most recent dataset is a portrayal of the present environment. So the knowledge must be grouped based on its relevance to the present environment, and be dynamically brought up to date as latest data arrives.
*   3\. The learner should have a system to resign itself when former and recently learned knowledge dispute with each other. Moreover, there should be a system for keeping track of both the incoming data and the learners performance on recent and existing data for the intention of complexity reduction, problematizing, and fading.
*   4\. The learner must have a system to neglect or omit information that is no longer relevant, but selectively with the added capability to look back such information if the drift or change chase a cyclical nature.
*   5\. Knowledge should be incrementally stored after certain chunk of time interval so that it can start working to generate the wise speculation for an unknown (or unlabeled) data instance through any instant of time in the learning routine.

Ensemble Techniques as a Solution for Concept Drift

Ensemble systems are also called as multiple classifier systems (MCS), have been designed and successfully carried out for learning in non-stationary environments . With each and every new dataset arrived, new classifiers are added and many times older one are removed to create an ensemble model to keep track of the environment. These methods generally go for a passive drift detection along with a fixed ensemble size (number of classifiers), where the most former member (e.g. Streets Streaming Ensemble Algorithm (SEA), and Bifets adaptive Hoeffding tree bagging) or the ensemble member which gives minimum performance (e.g.Tsymbals Dynamic Integration, Kolter and Maloofs, Dynamic Weighted Majority (DWM)) is substituted with a recent one. Although there are disagreements on which scheme to use for concept drift applications, for merging classifiers voting mechanism is preferred quite often.

Tsymbal merges a proximity measure with classifier performance to compute the voting weights, with classifiers whose training and test data are in the identical region of feature space being offered more weights . Gao, recommends simple majority voting, highlighting that weights based on classifier error on drifting data is not giving enough information for later datasets.Other versions of ensemble methods consists of . Hybrid methods that combine active detection, sliding windows and classifier ensembles have also been stated, such as random forests with entropy and Bifets novel integration of a Kalman filter merged with an adaptive sliding window algorithm, namely ADWIN.

Additionally there are many issues present in streaming data environment such as missing features in the data itself. The unity and completeness of data are necessary for any classification system. A trained classifier requires special training to address this challenge and cannot operate examples with lost characteristics. Missing data in real world applications is a common scenario: malfunctioning sensors, wrong pixel information, blank answers to questions asked in surveys, failed equipment, medical tests that cannot be monitored under some specific situations, etc. are all common applications in real-life that can result in lost characteristics. Values of features that are beyond certain dynamic minimum and maximum limit of the data caused by utmost noise, signal saturation, data corruption, etc. can also be considered as missing features. The simplest way to deal with such lost data is to neglect those instances that have missing attributes. When large portions of the data is facing problem of missing features or lost attributes filtering or deletion (list wise) are suboptimal (and impractical due to conditions applied on them to work well) approaches and generally known as filtering. A more realistic approach is imputation where missing values are filled with a meaningful calculation like mean or finding k-nearest neighbor value etc. to get correct estimates of missing values training data should be dense with enough number of features. Learn++.MF is an algorithm that attempts to extract the most unfair classification information stipulated by the present (old) data, so that it can take most benefit of duplication in the feature set. In other words, Learn++.MF do not have any concern with the estimation prediction of missing data values. Therefore, Learn++.MF prevents many of the demerits of estimation and imputation based approaches. This is a novel way to accommodate crucial amount of lost data values and without slow decline in performance as the volume of data grows.

SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

Hypothesis

*   H0: Unbalanced nature of data degrades the performance of classifier in credit card threat assessment.
*   H1: It is necessary to handle issue of non-stationary environment of credit risk evaluation model where concept drift is observed.

Let us assume credit card fraud detection system as use case for this system. In other words, the algorithmic framework is going to be applied on credit system to relinquish between faithful and fraudulent customers. As said earlier data usually found in machine learning environment can have different challenges such as concept drift, unbalancing, etc. Traditional machine learning theory presented in the classical texts generally have typical assumption that the learner algorithm classifying from a fixed yet unknown data distribution. Having this kind of assumption relating to data distribution may not be a valid thought when the data is raised from dynamic environments. While the classical texts stipulate quite detailed theory of machine learning approaches and solutions, they do not address the problems faced in many real world applications such as credit card fraud detection, spam email identification, weather forecasting etc. Concept drift happens when the statistical properties that observe the joint probability distribution get modified as a function of time. Class imbalance or unbalanced data refers to an unequal presence of classes in a pattern recognition scenario.

Desired properties of a joint framework for learning concept drift from imbalanced data are:

*   1\. Learning new knowledge.
*   2\. Preserving previous knowledge.
*   3\. One pass learning.
*   4\. Balance on minority/majority class performance.

ARCHITECTURAL VIEW

Let us turn the attention to actual architecture of the system. As seen in the literature review section, there are several algorithms present for each issue. But the system basically uses Learn++.NIE as a fundamental algorithm. However, for improvement of this base algorithm, we

have proposed a new way to use mapping function for weight distribution along with this framework so that it forms a joint solution to all the problems in incremental learning environment. The framework is named as MINE (Mapping function for Imbalanced and Non-stationary Environment). The general view of the system architecture is also given at the end. First the flow of each component is illustrated in detail. For the sake of simplicity of explanation, the system’s flow is divided into three phases. The description of each phase is as follows:

*   Phase 1: The very first phase includes basic input to the system, handling of class imbalance and weight updation module. The framework is fed up with input dataset, ensemble size (number of classifiers in the ensemble), error weights (typically value is in the range of 0 to 1), and sigmoidal parameters (a & b). Unbalanced training data is passed to bagging variation procedure to rebalance the instances. Then this balanced data is fed to weight modification mechanism. As discussed the weight updation module is developed using mapping function which in turn makes use of MLP deep learning network to populate weights in iterative manner. Here, the concept of deep learning is applied. The upper layer of logistic regression learning model only is formed with the help of MLP implementation. The system is trained and tested over several iterations in order to form required neural network.

Then, after some predetermined standard learning rate, it stops and produces some error values as weight measures. They are primarily called as epsilon (standard error) and beta (normalized error). Note that this error values are representation of drifts in the system. The differences in these values and corresponding analysis tells us about the concept drift occurred in the system. The basic mechanism of the mapping function is shown in Figure 2. Here, D[t] is dataset and P[t] is associated distribution function at a currant time instance t. It is then given to MLP and it predicts the initial distribution, this happens for several iterations.

*   Phase 2: Input to the phase 2 is nothing but the output of phase 1, i.e. weight measure values. Now, it is the time to determine whether the weight measure value is equals to currant time instance. If this question is answered as yes, then generate a new sun-ensemble, otherwise set the error (weight) values to be less than current time instance. After this, calculate beta value of the weight measure error as that is going to be used in subsequent steps. In the next component, calculate final error measure at currant time instance t. This phase performs critical mathematical steps and they all are needed to compute final classification decision. Phase 2 actually plays with several kinds of error values including epsilon and beta. This phase is especially useful for ensemble system implementation that we are using as solution to concept drift problem.
*   Phase 3: As the system implements ensemble technique, it is obvious that there are multiple classifiers, their individual hypothesis, and finally the composite hypothesis that gives the final classification decision. To compute this composite hypothesis one has to apply some kind of voting mechanism. Examples include majority voting, minority voting, probabilistic voting, sum rule, majority voting etc. Here, we have used majority voting technique to combine ensemble decisions. But before that computation of weighted sum of normalized error is mandatory since it is going to be one of the inputs for majority voting. Now, according to all previous calculations and phase traversal, the last step computes ultimate computation i.e. final classification decision and tells us that whether the customer belongs to faithful category or it is a fraud one.

MINE Framework Risk Analysis

As one can easily observe, the system is quite complex. But note that this is not a drawback of the system. Yes, it is the property of this framework since it addresses wide range of problems in single system. So if the efficiency requirement is more, data is unbalanced, concept drift and concept classes are major concerns, then definitely this is a complete solution for real world situations. As evolution of computers is grown in progressive way, todays computers are capable of handling this much complexity. Obviously, the nature and kind of input dataset determines how complex the system execution is going to be and how much time it’ll take. So the risk analysis is explained with the help of following points:

*   1\. Wide Swings in Error: Sometimes classifier may tend to produce error and it may have wide swings. Such swings leads to degraded performance of the algorithm. Hence, to control such swings, sigmoidal parameters ’a’ and ’b’ are used in this algorithmic framework. Ensemble strategy is used for classification which helps to reduce such errors.
*   2\. Misclassification of Instances: Credit card fraud detection system detects the fraud, means it identifies bad customer. Misclassification paves the path to bad performance since it increases the error rate. It means that good customers are identified as bad ones, or vice versa. This is not acceptable since this system is highly related to financial applications and errors are not acceptable in this area. MultiLayer Perceptron Neural Network is used for weight distribution in the proposed system and it is mainly focused to improve accuracy of the classification in this application.
*   3\. Increased Building Time and Evaluation Time of Model: If the data supplied is vast, and not preprocessed then time to build training model and testing model increases. Solution is to use standard dataset which is already preprocessed and number of instances are known and possibly less.

Optimization Issues

Major motive of the system is to optimize existing system. Optimization can be achieved by setting parameters of algorithms to standard threshold values which are obtained after several experiments. Some constraints can also be applied which does not affect performance and does not limits the system to specific area but it removes unnecessary complexity. As risk analysis section described the risks in the system, optimization concerns are the thought process which exactly works in reverse way. In other words, optimization is nothing but thinking of risk parameters and finding solutions on them. For example, setting of ensemble size to some value will prevent unnecessary proliferation of the classifiers and ultimately it is one of the biggest optimization that can be achieved in this system so far. One more thing to add here is that implementation of MINE framework itself implicitly takes care of some kind of basic preprocessing of training data like missing value problem. So, it is crystal clear that the system is quite familiar with all the optimization concerns and surely is able to deal with it.

RELEVANT MATHEMATICS

This section covers the relevant mathematics to the system. There are various formulas that are involved in the system for computation of specific parameters. Those formulas are listed out here along with the description of the variables and it’s purpose.

Error Computation

This formulas are actually used for weight measure computation in the system. All of them are not used at once. At a time only one of them is used to calculate distribution weights. They are actually various ways to compute weight measure and are iteratively refined in the successive runs of the system.F1 measure formula is used in the Learn++.NIE algorithm. among these 3 measures,F1 measure performs better, hence existing system (i.e. Learn++.NIE) prefers F1 measure formula over other two measures. This error metrics have to be used to accommodate class imbalance. They balance the algorithm on majority and minority classes using weight values for non-stationary environment.

*   1.
    
    F1 – Measure.
    
    E = 1 - F1
    
    F1 = 2 \*\[ (Precision\*recall) / (Precision + recall)\]
    
*   2.
    
    Geometric Mean.
    
    ![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch023.m03](i/ch023.m03.svg)
    

Geometric-mean is an indicator of classifier performance, whether the learner is performing across all classes or only on minority classes.

Here:

*   j: Class name.
*   Pk: Performance of sub ensemble at time t.
*   c: Number of classes.
*   3.Weighted Recall Measure.
    
    E= ή (1 - pk(+)) + (1 - ή) (1 - Pk(-))
    
*   ή: A threshold term that controls the weight assigned to a specific class error, possible values are only in the range of 0 to 1.
*   Pk(-): Majority class.
*   Pk(+): Minority class.

For balanced performance, default value of ή is assigned as 0.5 generally.

This measure explicitly balances precision and recall performance.

Performance Evaluation Measures

*   1.
    
    Accuracy: Accuracy is calculated by using correctly classified instances divided by total instances multiplied by 100.
    
    Accuracy = (TP + TN=TP + TN + FP + FN) \* 100
    

where,

*   TP: TruePositive.
*   TN: True Negative.
*   FP: False Positive.
*   FN: False Negative.

It is one of the most widely used and simple measure to assess algorithm performance, in simpler terms it tells us that the more accurate algorithm is better one in terms of performance.

EXPERIMENTS AND RESULTS

This section describes the experiments held and corresponding results in detail.

For simulation purpose, assumptions are:

*   • German Credit dataset is mainly used in the experiments from UCI repository and it consists of 1000 samples.
*   • Dataset is divided into 11 chunks of equal size approximately.
*   • Statistical nature of dataset is tested and is found to be discrete.

Since this MINE framework uses base classifier as CART, the results can be represented in the form of decision tree whereby leaf nodes will show the classes and intermediate nodes and path towards leaf node is modeled as complete conditions for the risk assessment. Consider an example, attribute values obtained as: checking status is <= 0, duration is < =11, foreign\_worker=yes, existing credits<=1, property magnitude = real estate, then class=good. Also, it will be useful for knowledge preservarance since mapping function leads to knowledge transfer by forming a mesh neural network from each instance of dataset to each other. The connections are very strong.

MINE FRAMEWORK: SYSTEM ANALYSIS

Factors considered for analysis of this system are as follows:

*   1\. Algorithmic parameters, e.g. ensemble size, T.
*   2\. Nature of Input data, e.g. Unbalanced distribution of instances.
*   3\. Time series.
*   4\. Size of Input data, e.g. large no. of instances leads to reduction in speed.
*   5\. Nature of environment (here, non-stationary).

It is mapped to standard problem- Travelling salesman problem(TSP) . The scenario is TSP is that, the salesperson has to visit certain cities for the sales and for that only the distance between two or more cities is considered for calculation. That distance in kilometres usually tells about the estimation of time and expenditure required. But in real world, the picture can be different and more difficult. For example, the condition of roads may be bad, the whether could go wrong at certain point of time, the salesperson have to unwillingly wait in a traffic jam, certain catastrophic condition could occur, and lot more situations. But is it necessary to consider all this possible situations while computation and solving of TSP? Certainly not. In other words, for the simplicity, and to solve the problem in polynomial time, the constraints are loosened up and only required and compulsory conditions are considered for the calculation. For small problems, even such conditions might be considered, but for really big problems, or real world algorithms, the calculation may stuck if all such conditions are considered. So, this is how, the system in this document is tried to co-relate with TSP whereby certain constraints are loosened up and the problem is solved in polynomial time. Stream data mining occurs when patterns must be extracted from noisy, loosely correlated data. Solving problems, even NP complete ones, on noise- and error-free data is, by comparison, easy. Imagine trying to solve a variant of the standard travelling salesman problem where instead of exact coordinates for the towns, you were given inaccurate estimates, given by random citizens surveyed in the streets. In order to get the best answer, you cannot only apply the standard algorithm; you must also form a judgement of the accuracy of each data point.

CONCLUSION

Credit card fraud detection needs to identify threats in transaction accurately. Since the environment of this problem is non-stationary with unbalanced data, there are certain challenges that should be addressed. Weight distribution computation of existing algorithm is improved by employing mapping function based on neural network that is more accurate, will lead to knowledge transformation and in turn will pave the path towards performance enhancement for credit risk assessment. The infinitely many variations of non-stationary environments that one can encounter make such an analysis a difficult proposition.

FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS

Scope of future work is leading towards an intelligent approach that will overcome limitations of the existing research body and also rigorously assessing these techniques on large scale, real world examples including formal statistical analyses of these algorithms, on certain non-stationary environments like Gaussian distribution drifts. The system can also be implemented in future by using advanced statistical packages in ‘R’ for making real world analytics of it. The practical use cases are aimed to be search and apply the research to find solutions of those problems and probably make a good software product to fulfill analytical needs of society.

KEY TERMS AND DEFINITIONS

Algorithm: A stepwise procedure which systematically performs some task to achieve required output.

Batch Learning: The data instances are grouped into a batch and then are processed at once. They are not processed instance wise.

Class Imbalance: Presence of less instances of one particular class as compared to another.

Classification: The task of grouping the data instances in various categories known as classes while going through training and testing phases.

Concept Drift: A change in the concept. Over the time period some class definitions may change due to dynamic nature of data distribution function and the nature of data and kind of application.

Credit Card Fraud Detection: Credit data may contain some classes which represents fraudulent transactions or bad customers, classifying this data into good customers and bad customers is the typical task of machine learning approaches.

Incremental Learning: Learning the data instances over the time period by preserving older ones and learning from new data. Here, the new data is learned instance wise and the older one is stored and preserved.

Non-Stationary Environment: An environment where sudden concept drift can occur due to dynamic and unknown probability data distribution function.

Supervised Learning: This is another name for classification since it performs its task with the help of some labeled data which it has obtained in advance to form a prediction model.

Unbalanced Data: The data which consists of class imbalance.

# Chapter 24

*   Junming Zhang  
    Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China
*   Jinglin Li  
    Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, China

ABSTRACT

Moving objects gathering pattern represents a group events or incidents that involve congregation of moving objects, enabling the analysis of traffic system. However, how to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the gathering pattern discovering method still remains as a challenging issue since the large number of moving objects will generate high volume of trajectory data. In order to address this issue, the authors propose a method to discovering the gathering pattern by analyzing the taxicab demand. This paper first introduces the concept of Taxicab Service Rate (TSR). In this method, they use the KS measures to test the distribution of TSR and calculate the mean value of the TSR of a certain time period. Then, the authors use a neural network based method Neural Network Gathering Discovering (NNGD) to detect the gathering pattern. The neural network is based on the knowledge of historical gathering pattern data. The authors have implemented their method with experiments based on real trajectory data. The results show the both effectiveness and efficiency of their method.

1\. INTRODUCTION

The increasing availability of location acquisition has been applied to GPS on vehicles. The technology has enabled tracking almost any moving behaviors of moving objects, which results in huge volumes of spatio-temporal data in the form of trajectories. Movement pattern can be observed from this kind of data. The movement pattern will provide useful information for traffic jam prediction and traffic flow control.

The movement pattern has been well studied for the past few years (L. Huang, Wang, Hsu, Zhang, & Yang, 2015; Jeung, Yiu, Zhou, Jensen, & Shen, 2010; Kalnis, Mamoulis, & Bakiras, 2005; Li, Ding, Han, & Kays, 2010; S. Wang, Hsu, Liang, Sun, & Yang, 2014; Zheng, Zheng, Yuan, & Shang, 2013) (Jeung, Yiu, Zhou, Jensen, & Shen, 2010). In order to support the traffic analysis application in cities, Zheng (Zheng et al., 2013) has proposed a useful movement pattern which name is gathering. It represents a behavior of a set of spatio-temporal moving objects, which move together within a certain period of time. The author has also proposed a gathering pattern discovery method by counting the gathering number. Specifically, it uses the spatial Gird to index the crowd of moving objects, and then uses the Crowd-TAD method to test each crowd to discover the gathering pattern. To improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the gathering pattern retrieving process, we have also proposed a gathering retrieving method based on spatio-temporal graph that forms by moving object clusters (Zhang JM, 2016). The main part of the method is to find the maximal complete graph that meets the spatio-temporal constraints by indexing the graph. But it still took a lot of time to cluster the moving objects and to search graph. Recently, some researchers use the taxicab demand to analyze the traffic condition or find a fast driving route (Liu, Zheng, Chawla, Yuan, & Xing, 2011; Ma, Zheng, & Wolfson, 2013; Rui, Hacker, & Rong, 2014; Yuan, Zheng, Xie, & Sun, 2011). Researcher (Yuan, Zheng, Zhang, Xie, & Sun, 2011) presented a recommender system by using the taxicab drivers’ pick-up behaviors. Our previous research has also proposed method to analyze the taxicab demand (Zhou, Zhang, Li, & Wang, 2014). From this point, we could use the taxicab demand to discover the gathering pattern. Even though it need to calculate the taxicab demand from the trajectory data, it will save a huge time comparing with the moving object clustering and graph searching process.

In this paper, we propose a method to retrieve the gathering pattern by analyzing the taxicab demand. This paper first introduces the concept of Taxicab Service Rate (TSR), which can reflect the real demand of taxicab in different regions. The method has two processes: TSR calculating and gathering pattern discovery. In the TSR calculating process, first, we segment the whole map to disjoint regions r bounded by the grid. Second, we use the KS measures to test the distribution of TSR at a certain time period. At last, we use an improved Parzen window method to estimate the Probability Density Function (PDF) of TSR and calculate the mean value of the TSR in a specific time period. In the gathering pattern detecting process, we use a neural network based method NNGD to detect the gathering pattern. Firstly, historical gathering pattern data are used to train the network. Then, we use a four-layer feed-forward network to classify the movement pattern to gathering pattern or non-gathering pattern. In this paper, we make the following contributions:

*   • This paper introduces a new point of view to discover the gathering pattern. Firstly, we use the Parzen window method to calculate the mean value of the TSR in a specific time period. Then neural network based method NNGD is used to discover the gathering pattern.
*   • This paper introduces the concept of TSR to measure the taxicab demand instead of the requests number, which is hard to count. Then, we use the KS measures to test the distribution of TSR at a certain time period. Lastly, the Parzen window method is introduced to estimate the PDF and calculate the mean value of TSR. In Parzen window method, an iteration algorithm has been used to get the most optimal window value and the mean value of TSR of a certain time period will be calculated by using the PDF.
*   • This paper uses a feed-forward neural network NNGD to detect the gathering pattern, which will detect whether the movement pattern is a gathering pattern or not. The historical gathering pattern data are used to train the network.
*   • Lastly we provide an experimental evaluation of our method and apply it to a large trajectory dataset. The effectiveness and efficiency outperforms other methods.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. The next section defines the necessary concepts and illustrates the framework of the proposed method in this paper. Effective solutions for PDF estimating and mean value calculating of TSR are presented in Section 3. The gathering pattern discovery method is showed in Section 4. Section 5 presents the simulation results. Related work concerning taxicab demand is discussed in Section 6. Finally, the conclusions are given in Section 7.

2\. PRELIMINARY

In this section, we define some terms used in this paper and give an overview of our method.

*   Definition 1 (Taxi Trajectory): A taxi trajectory Tr is a sequence of GPS points pertaining to one trip. Each point p consists of longitude p.x, latitude p.y, time stamp p.t and occupancy status p.s. That is, Tr:p[1]→p[2]→…→p[n], where each point p[i]\={(<p.x[i], p.y[i]\>, p[i].t, p[i].s)}, p[i]∈Tr.
*   Definition 2 (Region): The map of a city is partitioned into disjoint regions r bounded by the grid. Each region may consist of a number of road segments and lands.

Figure 1 is an example segmented map of Beijing. The map is segmented into 6×5 regions, where r[ij] (1≤i≤6, 1≤j≤5) is the region of the row i and column j.

*   Definition 3 (Taxicab Service Rate): Given the empty taxicab number C[e] at time t[i], the on service taxi number C[p] at time t[i+1], the taxicab service rate is p\=C[p]/C[e].

This paper aims to present a method that could discover the gathering pattern through taxicab demand. The method has two processes: TSR calculating and gathering pattern discovery.

3\. TAXICAB SERVICE RATE CALCULATION

In this section, we will present our method for modeling TSR distribution from a trajectory database. Basically, our method consists two parts: distribution testing and probability density function estimating. Firstly, we segment the digital map into n equal-sized regions, where each region is a rectangle, as shown in Figure 1. Each region of the map contains a large number of taxicab trajectory r[i]\={Tr[i]|Tr[i]∈Tr[DB]}, r[i]∈R[DB]. The details of this phase are omitted because it is easy to perform, and it finally outputs a database of trajectory T[DB]\={r[1], r[2], ... r[n]}.

In order to model the distribution of TSR, the first part aims to test the distribution of TSR and checks whether it follows the normal distribution, the second part proposes will use the Parzen window to estimate the PDF of TSR. In the next two subsections, we will elaborate our proposed techniques for modeling the TSR step by step.

3.1. Distribution Testing

The taxicab demand in a region is difficult to estimate, because we cannot get the real requests from passengers. Most researches choose to use the pick-up number of taxicab instead of the real requests. However, the demand estimated by this method cannot be accurate. For example, the region having large number of requests but fewer empty taxicabs, with the result that only a part of the passengers will be picked up. In order to solve this, we use TSR instead of the request number. TSR is the radio of on service taxicab number at time t[i+1] and empty taxicab number at t[i].

To start getting the TSR of one region r[1], we partition the trajectory of one day into 24 hours. Then for each minute t[m] in one hour, we can calculate the rate ![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch024.m01](i/ch024.m01.svg). The average TSR of two different time periods in one week is shown in Figure 4. It can be easily observed that TSR rarely changes in one minute. However, it will have a great variation between different hours. Intuitively, the distribution of TSR will follow the normal distribution in a time period. In the next paragraphs, we present the KS method to test the normality of the TSR distribution. The experimental results are shown in section 4.

To test the normality of request rate distribution, we use the KS (Kurtosis and Skewness) (Mardia, 1970) measures. Kurtosis (k) and Skewness (s) are the most widely used procedures for accessing distributional shape. The kurtosis coefficient has frequently been considered in the literature as a measure of peakness and flatness, which is defined below:

The value of k\=0 means that the data show the same kurtosis as a normal distribution, whereas positive values are interpreted as being more peaked and negative ones as flatter than the normal.

The Skewness metric indicates whether the peak of one distribution is symmetric or skewed to one side, which is defined below:

![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch024.m04](i/ch024.m04.svg)

The value of s=0 indicates a symmetrical shape, positive values mean that the curve is skewed to the right (right-tail), and negative values suggest skewing to the left (left-tail).

Finally, we can test the normality by testing Kurtosis and Skewness. In (Mardia, 1970), the authors propose a metric that can be used to test the normality of TSR distribution. The distribution follows the normal distribution if:

4\. GATHERING PATTERN DISCOVERY

In order to facilitate understanding the method, we first give the structure of method as shown in Figure 3. The process can be divided into two phases as shown in Figure 3, the first phase is the training phase and second phase is the detecting phase. During the training phase, the method generates a training set by using the gathering pattern data, which will be used to train the network. In the detecting phase, the network will detect the gathering pattern which based on the knowledge of historical gathering pattern data.

4.1. Neural Network Training

In this subsection, we introduce the training part of the method. Specifically, we use a modified back propagation (BP) algorithm in the training phase. The back propagation learning algorithm is recognized as a supervised learning algorithm. Here we use it as the training algorithm to train a network.

Given N initial learning samples of the network, they are clustered into 2 categories, one for similar samples and the other one for dissimilar samples. The difference between similar samples and dissimilar samples is that the target result of similar samples is 1 but 0 in dissimilar samples.

The training algorithm is the gradient descent with momentum and adaptive learning rate back propagation which can train any network as long as its weight, network input, and transfer functions have derivative functions. This algorithm is a network training function that updates weights and bias values according to gradient descent momentum and adaptive learning rate. In order to minimize the error produced by the given attributes and the target attributes, following steps have to go through:

*   Step 1:
    
    Calculating error function:

where o[i] is the expected output value. When we send a training set P\={(x[1], t[1]),…, (x[n], t[n])} to the network, it produces an output set S\={s[1],…, s[n]} for every input data type x[i] in the training set, where (x[i], t[i]) is the training pair of the data type, s[i] is similarity result for each input (x[i], t[i]).

*   Step 2:
    
    Minimizing E by calculating the gradient of error function:
    
    ![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch024.m23](i/ch024.m23.svg)
    

Each weight is updated using the increment:

![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch024.m24](i/ch024.m24.svg)

where γ is a learning constant, a proportionally parameter which defines the step length of each iteration in the negative gradient direction, w[i] represents the weights of the links in the network. Based on the above given steps the derivatives of error function for neural network layers can be recurrently calculated. Then the output error propagates back through the hidden layer to the input layer so that the weights of the links will be optimized.

4.2. Gathering Pattern Detecting

In this subsection, a feed forward neural network is used to detect the gathering pattern. The feed-forward neural networks, which have multiple layers, are constructed by ordered units. The units can always be arranged in layers so that connections go from one layer to a later layer. The algorithm uses a four-layer network: one input layer, two hidden layers and one output layers. In order to detect the gathering pattern of a specific location x, the algorithm will obtain the mean value of TSR of 4 regions around x and present them to the input layer.

Now let us describe the feed-forward neural network. Thus, the 4 units in input layer represent the TSR of 4 regions, the 1 unit in output layer refers to the output similarity value, and the hidden layer is used to reduce the noise of the network. The transformation from input unit x[i] to output unit y[k], which can be absorbed into weights, is described as:

![Mathtype978-1-7998-0414-7.ch024.m25](i/ch024.m25.svg)

where the f[0] and f[h] function are almost taken to be linear, logistic (with f(x)=l(x)=e^x/(1+e^x)) or threshold functions. The links from input layer to hidden layer have the weights w[ij], which is generated randomly. It is same to the links from hidden layer to output layer.

5\. EXPERIMENTS

In this section, we conduct the experiments on a real trajectory data. The experiments can be divided into two parts. The first part is on testing the effectiveness and the second part is to test the efficiency of our method.

5.1. Experimental Settings

The dataset¹ that contains one month trajectory data generated by GPS devices installed on taxicabs in the city of Beijing. The trajectory is a sequence of points which contains taxicab ID, trigger event (0 for empty, 1 for with passenger), operational status (same as trigger event), time point, GPS (Longitude, Latitude), taxicab velocity, direction(from 000 to 360 in degree), and GPS status (0 for invalid, 1 for valid). The example of the data set is listed in Table 1. The whole map of Beijing was limited to \[(116.0800, 39.6811), (116.7721, 40.1777)\] so that extreme outliers can be removed and the map was segmented to 900 regions. In the experiments we choose 5 regions that most trips are consistent.

5.2. The Effectiveness Test

This section will test the effectiveness of the gathering pattern discovering. We will give three set of experiments. The first is to test the normality of the TSR. The second is to estimate the PDF of TSR. The last is to show the effectiveness of our method.

5.2.1. Normality Testing

We first evaluate the normality testing results of our method for taxicab request rates. In the first experiment, we obtain the request rates of five different regions in a week. Then, the rates in one day are divided into three kinds of time period: one hour, two-hour and three-hour. We use the KS measure to test normality of different time periods. Figure 5 shows the average normality number of one day in a week. We can see that the distribution of request rate is normal in most of the time period. That implies the request rates change a little in one hour. It is obvious that the normality of one hour is higher than other time periods. It is because the request of taxicab will change with time. For example, people tend to take a taxi to their office at morning, but most of them will stay there until they are off work. It is also notice that the number of two-hour is higher than three-hour. The main reason is that the request will change more if we enlarge the time period. We also note an interesting result that the normality number of region r[1] is the highest. It is because the size of trajectory data in region r[4] is more than other regions. So, the sample size is large, the distribution is more approximate to normal distribution.

In Figure 6, the results show that the normality number in week day is higher than weekend. That is because the patterns of most people tend to be regular on weekdays. On the contrary, most of people will take a taxi any time of the day at weekends. Some people will probably go shopping at 10:00am and return at 10:00pm, but some of them will follow the same patterns as on weekdays. It causes a variability of request between different people. Then, we test the average normality number of Saturday and Sunday in the same parameters. As shown in Figure 7, the number of normality hours in Saturday is higher than in Sunday. The main reason is that most people will also work overtime on Saturday. It is also noticed that the normality hours of region r[4] in Figure 6 and Figure 7 are almost the same. The main reason is that the size of trajectory data is the largest. The requests will reach the equilibrium point if the sample data is large enough.
